title: Extremist, Hate-Group and High-Control Movement Atlas
scope: Public-source research layer for organizations and movements that are designated, documented or widely studied as hate groups, extremist organizations, terrorist organizations, armed movements, or high-control/destructive religious movements.
method: The atlas separates designation from description. A group can be hateful without being armed; armed without being a hate group; high-control without being classified as a hate group; inactive without disappearing from historical influence. Membership counts are included only when credible public estimates exist. No private member identities, home addresses, tactical instructions or operational security information are stored.
fields: Each record tracks aliases, status, geography at country/region level, ideology or target category, public membership evidence, affiliations, violence/arms status at a high level, and source provenance.

records.name: Ku Klux Klan (KKK)
records.status: fragmented; multiple current and historical organizations
records.targets_or_hate: Black Americans, Jews, immigrants, Catholics, LGBTQ+ people and other groups depending on faction and period
records.membership: No reliable single current membership total; modern Klan activity is fragmented into small organizations.
records.armed_or_violent: Historically associated with organized racial terrorism and violence. Current factions vary; historical violence should not be projected onto every present-day individual member.
records.affiliations: Multiple independent Klan organizations; no single centralized KKK governing body.
records.notes: Treat the KKK as a family of organizations rather than one contemporary corporation.

records.name: Patriot Front
records.targets_or_hate: Immigrants and racial/ethnic minorities; promotes white-nationalist and exclusionary nationalism
records.membership: Public sources do not provide a reliable complete membership census; activity is assessed through demonstrations, propaganda and identified chapters.
records.armed_or_violent: Militant street-activist organization; public research documents confrontational demonstrations. This field does not infer individual weapon possession.
records.affiliations: Emerged from Vanguard America; part of broader U.S. white-nationalist ecosystem.
records.notes: Track as an organization/network, not as a synonym for every nationalist or conservative organization.

records.name: Active Club Network
records.targets_or_hate: White-supremacist ideology; opposition to racial pluralism and immigration
records.membership: Distributed chapter network; ADL reported activity in at least 25 U.S. states and multiple chapters abroad in its backgrounder.
records.armed_or_violent: Members train physically and some chapters emphasize a 'warrior' identity; the network should not be treated as a conventional armed force.
records.affiliations: Inspired by Rise Above Movement (R.A.M.) and connected to other white-supremacist networks.
records.notes: Useful model for studying decentralized coupling rather than assuming centralized command.

records.name: Blood Tribe
records.targets_or_hate: Jews, Black people, immigrants, LGBTQ+ people and other groups targeted by neo-Nazi ideology
records.membership: No reliable public census; public activity is tracked through demonstrations, propaganda and investigations.
records.armed_or_violent: Extremist organization with a violent ideological orientation in public reporting; no operational weapons information is included here.
records.affiliations: Part of the contemporary neo-Nazi ecosystem and overlapping with other white-power networks.
records.notes: Keep ideology, public activity and criminal allegations in separate evidence fields.

records.name: Aryan Brotherhood
records.targets_or_hate: Racial minorities and rival groups; ideology combines white supremacy with criminal organization
records.membership: Public estimates vary substantially by faction and source; no single audited membership figure.
records.armed_or_violent: Violent prison-gang history and criminal activity are extensively documented; this atlas records the status without operational detail.
records.affiliations: Multiple related prison-gang organizations use the Aryan Brotherhood name; they should not automatically be treated as one organization.
records.notes: Name collisions are a major graph-integrity problem: similarly named prison gangs may be independent.

records.name: Aryan Brotherhood of Texas
records.targets_or_hate: Racial minorities and rival prison/criminal groups
records.membership: Historical public estimates have placed membership in the thousands, but current numbers are uncertain.
records.armed_or_violent: Violence and weapons-related criminal conduct have been documented in prosecutions and investigative reporting.
records.affiliations: Independent organization; not simply a local chapter of every organization called Aryan Brotherhood.
records.notes: Use distinct node IDs for distinct prison organizations.

records.name: National Socialist Movement (NSM)
records.targets_or_hate: Jews, Black people, immigrants and other groups targeted by National Socialist ideology
records.membership: No reliable current census; historically a small national network with local chapters.
records.armed_or_violent: Militant ideology; public evidence of individual weapons or violence should be attached case-by-case rather than generalized.
records.affiliations: Broader neo-Nazi and white-power ecosystem.
records.notes: Status should be timestamped because small extremist groups frequently rename or fragment.

records.name: American Front
records.status: historically active; current status requires timestamped verification
records.targets_or_hate: Racial minorities, immigrants and Jews
records.membership: No reliable current public total.
records.armed_or_violent: Extremist street movement with a documented history of violent rhetoric and incidents; do not infer current weapons possession.
records.affiliations: White-power and racist-skinhead ecosystem.
records.notes: Keep historical listings distinct from proof of current operational activity.

records.name: Three Percenters / III% movement
records.status: decentralized movement; activity varies by chapter
records.targets_or_hate: Anti-government and anti-authority ideology; rhetoric can overlap with anti-immigrant and conspiracy movements
records.membership: No reliable central membership count because the movement is decentralized and label-based.
records.armed_or_violent: Militia movement associated with armed self-defense/paramilitary imagery. Individual chapter or member conduct must be assessed separately.
records.affiliations: Overlaps with militia, sovereign-citizen and other anti-government networks.
records.notes: A movement label is not equivalent to one legal entity.

records.name: Oath Keepers
records.status: severely diminished after federal prosecutions; network remnants may persist
records.targets_or_hate: Anti-government ideology and conspiracy narratives
records.membership: Historically claimed large membership, but credible active membership is uncertain and far below promotional claims.
records.armed_or_violent: Militia organization with armed-member culture; multiple leaders/members were convicted in connection with January 6, 2021.
records.affiliations: Broader militia and anti-government movement.
records.notes: Do not treat historical membership claims as current active membership.

records.name: Proud Boys
records.targets_or_hate: Anti-left, anti-immigrant and exclusionary nationalist rhetoric; documented extremist associations vary by chapter and period
records.membership: No reliable current census; organization has fragmented after prosecutions and leadership disruption.
records.armed_or_violent: Members have participated in political violence and street confrontations; individual weapon status is not inferred.
records.affiliations: Overlaps with broader far-right street networks and some militia actors.
records.notes: The graph should distinguish the organization from unrelated people who merely use similar rhetoric.

records.name: Atomwaffen Division
records.targets_or_hate: Jews, minorities, LGBTQ+ people and perceived political enemies
records.membership: Small network; no reliable current membership census.
records.armed_or_violent: Accelerationist network associated with violent plots and criminal cases; this atlas records the high-level status only.
records.affiliations: Linked historically to National Socialist Order and other accelerationist networks.
records.notes: Important example of why alias, successor and dissolution fields are required.

records.name: National Socialist Order
records.targets_or_hate: Neo-Nazi accelerationist targets and racial/religious minorities
records.membership: No reliable public total.
records.armed_or_violent: Violent extremist ideology documented by monitoring organizations; no tactical information stored.
records.affiliations: Successor/rebrand associated with Atomwaffen Division lineage.
records.notes: Alias history should connect this node to Atomwaffen rather than duplicating it.

records.name: Order of Nine Angles (O9A)
records.targets_or_hate: Extremist occult and neo-Nazi currents; advocacy materials include violence and antisemitic themes
records.membership: No reliable public membership census; network is decentralized and pseudonymous.
records.armed_or_violent: Associated with violent extremist ideology and criminal cases involving adherents; no operational guidance included.
records.affiliations: Has influenced or overlapped with some neo-Nazi and accelerationist circles.
records.notes: Study as an ideology/network rather than a conventional organization.

records.name: Westboro Baptist Church
records.targets_or_hate: LGBTQ+ people, Jews, Catholics, Muslims and others targeted by the group's theology
records.membership: Historically reported as a small group centered heavily on the Phelps family; no reliable current census.
records.armed_or_violent: Known primarily for provocative demonstrations and hateful expression rather than an armed movement.
records.affiliations: Independent church; closely tied historically to the Phelps family.
records.notes: Important example of a hate-group designation that does not imply armed activity.

records.name: Contemporary Nazi / neo-Nazi network (umbrella record)
records.status: active as a broad ideological field
records.targets_or_hate: Jews, Roma, Black people, immigrants, LGBTQ+ people and political opponents depending on organization
records.membership: No meaningful single membership number; this is an umbrella node, not an organization.
records.armed_or_violent: Some constituent organizations have violent histories; others are propaganda networks. Each child node requires separate assessment.
records.affiliations: Includes many independent organizations and online networks.
records.notes: Umbrella records should never be used to claim that every constituent group is identical.

records.name: Peoples Temple
records.targets_or_hate: Not best modeled as a conventional hate group; high-control dynamics, authoritarian leadership and coercion are central research topics.
records.membership: Thousands attended at its peak; Jonestown community numbered in the thousands before the 1978 mass death.
records.armed_or_violent: Armed guards and coercive control were present at Jonestown; ended in mass murder-suicide in 1978.
records.affiliations: Founded and led by Jim Jones; political relationships in California formed part of its historical context.
records.notes: Historical high-control case; avoid collapsing every religious commune into this model.

records.name: Aum Shinrikyo
records.status: defunct under original organization; successor groups exist
records.targets_or_hate: Apocalyptic worldview and perceived enemies of the movement
records.membership: Reached tens of thousands across Japan and overseas at its peak; current successor membership differs.
records.armed_or_violent: Developed chemical weapons and carried out the 1995 Tokyo subway sarin attack; this is historical record, not operational guidance.
records.affiliations: Successor groups include Aleph and Hikari no Wa, with differing public positions and legal treatment.
records.notes: Excellent case for linking ideology, organizational capacity, technology and violence without sensationalism.

records.name: Heaven's Gate
records.targets_or_hate: Not primarily a hate group; apocalyptic extraterrestrial theology and strict communal control are the relevant research dimensions.
records.membership: Dozens of members participated in the 1997 mass death.
records.armed_or_violent: Not an armed movement; the defining historical event was the 1997 mass suicide.
records.affiliations: Led by Marshall Applewhite and Bonnie Nettles.
records.notes: Use as a high-control/apocalyptic case, not a hate-group node.

records.name: Branch Davidians
geography: United States; Waco, Texas historical center
records.targets_or_hate: Not inherently a hate-group category; internal authority, apocalyptic interpretation and state conflict are key research topics.
records.membership: Historical membership at Mount Carmel was in the dozens; broader Davidian traditions are larger and diverse.
records.armed_or_violent: The 1993 Waco siege involved firearms and resulted in deaths; this does not describe every Branch Davidian community.
records.affiliations: Davidian Seventh-day Adventist lineage; David Koresh led the Mount Carmel community involved in the 1993 siege.
records.notes: Distinguish the 1993 Koresh group from broader Davidian religious history.

records.name: Fundamentalist Latter-day Saint movements (FLDS and related groups)
records.targets_or_hate: Not principally a hate-group category; research focuses on authority, plural marriage, gender hierarchy, communal control and alleged abuses in particular communities.
records.membership: Varies by organization; no single FLDS-wide census is reliable.
records.armed_or_violent: Not accurately characterized as an armed movement; criminal conduct must be assessed at the individual/community level.
records.affiliations: Includes FLDS and other independent fundamentalist Latter-day Saint-derived communities; they are not one organization.
records.notes: Avoid treating all Latter-day Saint traditions as one movement.

records.name: NXIVM
records.status: defunct as original organization after prosecutions
records.targets_or_hate: Not a hate group; coercive control, exploitation and criminal enterprise are the relevant categories.
records.membership: Had thousands of participants/customers over its history, but the inner DOS structure was much smaller.
records.armed_or_violent: Not an armed movement; leaders were convicted of serious crimes including racketeering and sex trafficking.
records.affiliations: Founded by Keith Raniere; DOS operated inside the broader NXIVM structure.
records.notes: Useful case for distinguishing a large public-facing organization from a small coercive inner network.

records.name: Shincheonji Church of Jesus
records.targets_or_hate: Not properly classified as a hate group; controversy concerns secrecy, recruitment practices, leadership and doctrinal exclusivity.
records.membership: The movement publicly claims a large international membership; independent estimates vary.
records.armed_or_violent: No basis for classifying it as an armed movement.
records.affiliations: Independent Christian new religious movement founded by Lee Man-hee.
records.notes: The atlas labels allegations as allegations rather than converting controversy into fact.

records.name: Church of Scientology
records.targets_or_hate: Not properly classified as a hate group; high-control classification is contested and should be documented as a scholarly/community debate.
records.membership: The organization and outside researchers provide widely divergent estimates; no universally accepted current figure.
records.armed_or_violent: Not an armed movement.
records.affiliations: International Church of Scientology network and related organizations.
records.notes: Important example where 'cult' is a contested descriptor rather than a settled legal category.

records.name: Independent high-control church cases
records.targets_or_hate: Varies
records.membership: Not applicable
records.armed_or_violent: Not applicable
records.affiliations: Not applicable
records.notes: Reserved as a methodology node for comparing high-control indicators without declaring every controversial church a cult.

status_taxonomy.active: credible public evidence of current organizational activity
status_taxonomy.fragmented: legacy organization or label persists through multiple independent groups
status_taxonomy.historical: important historical organization without reliable evidence of current operation
status_taxonomy.defunct: organization ceased as the original entity
status_taxonomy.successor: new entity continues some lineage or ideology
status_taxonomy.contested: status or classification disputed; preserve competing sources

armed_taxonomy.none_known: no credible basis to classify the organization as armed
armed_taxonomy.militant: uses militant/paramilitary culture or imagery without establishing a conventional armed force
armed_taxonomy.armed_history: credible historical evidence of organized weapons/violence
armed_taxonomy.armed_network: public evidence supports an organized armed or paramilitary structure
armed_taxonomy.case_specific: weapons/violence allegations require individual case records

graph_rules: Never equate designation by one monitoring organization with a universal legal judgment.
Never infer current membership from historical peak membership.
Never infer that every member shares every statement made by a leader.
Never publish private member identities or precise residential locations.
Connect successor organizations through explicit predecessor/successor edges.
Connect aliases without merging genuinely independent organizations.
Keep hate targets, ideology, criminal conduct, armed status and high-control allegations as separate dimensions.
Record source date because extremist networks rename, dissolve and re-form quickly.
